title: 2-wire and 4-wire transmitters
summary: Who powers a current loop: loop-powered 2-wire transmitters need a supplied loop, separately powered 4-wire transmitters need a passive input.

sections.heading: Loop-powered and separately powered
sections.body:
A **2-wire** (loop-powered) transmitter has only the two loop wires. It takes its own power from the loop and regulates the loop current between 4 and 20 mA, which is why 4 mA is the lowest valid signal. Something must drive that current: an analog input that supplies the loop, or an external loop supply in series.

A **4-wire** transmitter has a separate power supply and drives the loop current itself, so it needs a **passive** input that only measures. (A 3-wire device shares one conductor between supply and signal.)

sections.heading: In PLC Lab and on real modules
sections.body: In PLC Lab's generic model a current input either supplies the loop (for 2-wire devices) or is passive (for 4-wire devices), set per channel in the hardware configuration; the wrong combination carries no valid loop current. Real modules solve this differently: some provide separate terminals for 2-wire and 4-wire devices, some need an external loop supply, and connecting an active source to a supplied input can damage the transmitter or the module. Always follow the module and transmitter manuals.
